Applying that identical rule here: the domain directory is docs/ops/portfolio/ (where the parent product authority and its batch test manifest already live), the mission title PORTFOLIO-PF1-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY-R1 supplies the stem PORTFOLIO_PF1 and the type EXECUTION_AUTHORITY, and the version is the first materialization, 1.0.0.

how_new_controls_are_frozen_without_fork.resolution: They are frozen in THIS artifact, under the reserved prefix PF1-, in the PF1_NEW_CONTROLS block. The batch manifest remains the sole contract for every id it defines; this authority defines only strictly-new ids and redefines none.

APPROVED_RUN_CONTRACT.population_rule: For each member project, select THE MOST RECENT APPROVED ELIGIBLE RUN: a run with status = 'calculated' that has at least one row in sroi_run_reviews with status = 'approved' for that calculation_run_id and the same organization, ordered by run version DESC then calculated_at DESC. Inherited verbatim from the parent's aggregate_contract.population.

ordering_of_operations.rule: APPROVAL FILTERING OCCURS BEFORE LATEST-RUN SELECTION.
ordering_of_operations.consequence_frozen: A newer calculated but unapproved run MUST NOT displace an older approved run. The unapproved run is not a candidate at the moment the latest-run choice is made; it is not selected and then rejected.
ordering_of_operations.why_this_must_be_stated_as_an_ordering: The two orderings are indistinguishable on a population where every run is approved, and differ only where the newest run is unapproved. An implementation that filters after selecting would return no_approved_run for a project that in fact has an older approved run, which the parent's later_ineligible_runs key forbids: a more recent ineligible run 'never substitutes for the approved run'.

required_predicates: sroi_calculation_runs.project_id IN the portfolio's member projects
an EXISTS correlation to sroi_run_reviews on calculation_run_id with status = 'approved'
sroi_run_reviews.organization_id = the same organization as the run — organization correlation is required on the review side as well as the run side, never only on the run side

determinism_of_run_selection.claim: Ordering by run version DESC is already total per project.
determinism_of_run_selection.measured_evidence: db/migrations/0029_integrity.sql:6-7 creates `uq_sroi_run_project_version` as a UNIQUE INDEX on sroi_calculation_runs (project_id, version). At most one run exists per (project, version), so version DESC admits no tie within a project and the inherited calculated_at DESC clause is a defensive second key that cannot be reached through this uniqueness.
determinism_of_run_selection.reader_hazard: This uniqueness is NOT visible in db/schema.ts. The Drizzle table's constraint array at db/schema.ts:855-858 declares only the status check and idx_sroi_calculation_runs_project_id. A reviewer who verifies uniqueness against the schema module alone will wrongly conclude there is none; the constraint lives only in the migration.

APPROVED_REVIEW_TIEBREAK.rule: When the selected run has more than one row in sroi_run_reviews whose CURRENT status is 'approved', select the most recently created approved review: ORDER BY sroi_run_reviews.created_at DESC, sroi_run_reviews.id DESC.
APPROVED_REVIEW_TIEBREAK.total_tiebreaker: sroi_run_reviews.id is the total deterministic tie-breaker. It is a uuid PRIMARY KEY (db/schema.ts:910), so it is unique and NOT NULL, and the two-key ordering therefore admits no residual tie.

prohibited_ordering.reason_1_nullable: reviewed_at is declared `timestamp('reviewed_at')` at db/schema.ts:927 with no .notNull(), so it is NULLABLE.
prohibited_ordering.reason_2_null_ordering: PostgreSQL places NULLs FIRST under DESC by default. An approved review that was never stamped therefore wins over one that was, which is the opposite of 'most recent'.
prohibited_ordering.contrast_with_created_at: created_at is declared `timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull()` at db/schema.ts:928 — NOT NULL with a server default, so every row has one and the ordering is total in combination with id.

what_the_selected_review_supplies: included[].reviewId — the reviewId reported in the traceability tuple is the id of THIS review.
the preserved legacy manual readiness value associated with the selected run and review — see READINESS.

live_defect_this_corrects.statement: This is not a preference between two acceptable orderings. The live implementation orders reviews by the prohibited column.
live_defect_this_corrects.measured_evidence: lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:221 reads `.orderBy(desc(sroiRunReviews.reviewedAt))`, and lines 222-226 take the first row per calculation_run_id into readinessByRunId. Because reviewed_at is nullable and DESC sorts NULLs first, an unstamped review currently outranks a stamped one.

LEGACY_EXCLUSION.rule: Mandatory FIBC-042 exclusion. A project is excluded with reason `legacy_non_authoritative` when projects.governance_regime = 'pre_pc01b' OR the SELECTED sroi_calculation_runs.methodology_version IS NULL.
LEGACY_EXCLUSION.derivation_source: Persisted facts only, never inferred. Inherited verbatim from the parent's aggregate_contract.exclusion_reasons.legacy_non_authoritative.
LEGACY_EXCLUSION.which_run_is_tested: The SELECTED run — the approved-eligible run chosen by APPROVED_RUN_CONTRACT — not the newest run and not any other run of the project. Testing an unselected run's methodology_version would exclude or admit a project on the basis of a run that contributes nothing.
LEGACY_EXCLUSION.approval_does_not_override: An approved review does NOT override the legacy exclusion. A pre-PC-01B run with a currently-approved review is still excluded as legacy_non_authoritative. Approval establishes methodological review; it does not retro-fit a methodology version onto a run that predates versioning.
LEGACY_EXCLUSION.methodology_version_null_semantics: db/schema.ts:844-849 records that methodology_version is NULL on every run created before FIBIU-02, that the NULL is permanent and means 'predates versioning', and that it is never backfilled (IMPOSSIBLE_TO_BACKFILL). The exclusion therefore reads a stable permanent fact, not a transient gap awaiting a migration.

EXCLUSION_PRECEDENCE.semantics: Evaluation is first-match-wins in exactly this order. A project qualifying for more than one reason reports the earliest reason in the list and no other.
EXCLUSION_PRECEDENCE.no_seventh_reason: The set is closed at six. PF1 may not add a seventh reason, may not merge two, and may not rename one. The six are identical to the parent's aggregate_contract.exclusion_reasons key set; this authority adds only the evaluation order over that set.
EXCLUSION_PRECEDENCE.why_legacy_precedes_currency_and_ratio: legacy_non_authoritative is a governance-regime fact about whether the run may contribute to an authoritative aggregate at all. Reporting non_usd_currency or no_sroi_ratio for a pre-PC-01B run would describe a mechanical property of a run that was never eligible on governance grounds, and would make the FIBC-042 exclusion invisible in the excluded[] output wherever a legacy run also happens to be non-USD.

type_widening_required.prohibition: The union must remain a closed literal union. It may not be widened to `string`, which would let a seventh reason enter without a type error.

FORMULA.rule: portfolioSroiRatio = SUM(net social value) / SUM(total investment) over exactly the included population, computed with the current decimal arithmetic.
FORMULA.arithmetic: decimal.js, as already imported at lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:8 and used at :59-60, :81-82 and :92-94. PF1 changes the POPULATION that enters the sum; it does not change the arithmetic library, the accumulation order or the division.
FORMULA.same_universe_rule: Numerator and denominator are drawn from the SAME universe. An excluded project contributes to NEITHER the numerator nor the denominator — never a zero in the denominator, never a zero in the numerator.

POSTGRES_CONTRACT.matrix_is_a_floor: The packet requires this matrix 'at least'. PF1 may add further real-PostgreSQL cases within the two authorized PostgreSQL paths; it may not drop or weaken a row.

The batch manifest docs/ops/portfolio/PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_V1_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json remains the binding test contract for every id it defines. This authority cites those ids and adds five strictly-new ids under the disjoint PF1- prefix.
MANIFEST_DISPOSITION.precedent: COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_CE1_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json's MANIFEST_DISPOSITION, applied to a structurally identical situation. See ARTIFACT_FORM.

shared_with_other_nodes.disposition: Binding on PF1 to the extent of PF1's own paths and queries. PF1 discharges its share; the remainder of each control is discharged by PF2 or PF3. PF1 may not be recorded as having closed any of these ids outright.

explicitly_not_pf1.disposition: PF2 or PF3 obligations. PF1 neither implements nor stubs them, and their absence from a PF1 run is correct.

MANIFEST_DISPOSITION.exit_gates_note: These are the IMPLEMENTATION node's exit gates, inherited by PF1 from the batch manifest's exit_gates array. They are not the gates of the present authority-only mission, which are recorded separately under VALIDATION_PERFORMED_BY_THIS_MISSION.

PF1_NEW_CONTROLS.namespace_rule: Every id in this block begins with 'PF1-'. The prefix is reserved for this authority. Measured disjointness: the batch manifest's 55 ids use only the prefixes POS, NEG, MUT and SENT, and none begins with 'PF1-'.

positive_controls.description: For a selected run carrying two or more rows in sroi_run_reviews whose current status is 'approved', the aggregate reports as included[].reviewId the id of the review with the greatest created_at, and where two approved reviews share a created_at value, the greatest id. The associated legacy manual readiness value displayed is the one belonging to that same review.
positive_controls.fixture_requirement: At least one pair of approved reviews sharing an identical created_at, so that the id tiebreaker is actually exercised and not merely present in the ORDER BY. At least one approved review whose reviewed_at is NULL and whose created_at is the OLDEST, so that a reviewed_at-based ordering would select it and a created_at-based ordering would not.

negative_controls.description: sroi_run_reviews.reviewed_at is never an ordering input on any PF1 path. No PF1 authorized file contains an orderBy over reviewedAt or an ORDER BY over reviewed_at, in either the application query or any committed probe SQL.
negative_controls.why_a_static_control_is_appropriate: The ordering column is a syntactic property of the query. A static assertion over the five authorized paths catches a reintroduction that a fixture-based test would catch only when a fixture happens to distinguish the two orderings.
negative_controls.scope_boundary: Scoped to the five PF1 authorized paths. It makes no claim about reviewed_at usage elsewhere in the repository, where the column has legitimate uses.

mutation_controls.description: Moving the approval filter to AFTER latest-run selection — selecting each project's newest calculated run first and only then discarding it if it lacks an approved review — makes NEG-AGG-2 and PG-PF1-03 fail: a project whose newest run is unapproved but which has an older approved run is wrongly reported as no_approved_run, and the aggregate loses that project's contribution.
mutation_controls.non_vacuity_basis: The fixture required by PG-PF1-03 contains a project whose newest calculated run is unapproved and whose second-newest is approved. On that fixture the two orderings produce different includedCount and different portfolioSroiRatio values, so the mutation is observable arithmetically and not only by inspection.

mutation_controls.description: Replacing ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC with ORDER BY reviewed_at DESC on the approved-review selection makes PF1-POS-TIEBREAK-1 and PG-PF1-05 fail: the review with a NULL reviewed_at sorts first under PostgreSQL's default DESC NULLs-first rule and supplies the wrong reviewId and the wrong legacy readiness value.
mutation_controls.non_vacuity_basis: The mutated form is the form the live tree carries today at lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:221, so this control asserts a real correction rather than guarding a hypothetical regression. The fixture requirement in PF1-POS-TIEBREAK-1 guarantees the two orderings disagree.

mutation_controls.description: Letting a run whose total_investment is null, zero or negative collapse into reason no_run — rather than being excluded with reason zero_or_invalid_investment — makes NEG-AGG-6 and PG-PF1-09 fail. The project's exclusion reason is wrong, and a reader cannot distinguish a project that was never calculated from one whose calculated run carries an unusable investment.
mutation_controls.non_vacuity_basis: This is the live behaviour for the null case. lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:133-136 returns null from toProjectRunSummaryRun when the parsed investment is null, and :65-67 then classifies a null run as no_run. The zero and negative cases are worse than that today: they are neither null nor rejected, so they currently pass the guard and contribute a zero or a negative to the denominator. The mutation therefore reverts to a state that is observably present in the tree.
mutation_controls.boundary: This control does not authorize changing what toProjectRunSummaryRun does with a genuinely unparseable numeric column. It requires only that null, zero and negative investment on an otherwise valid selected run be reported as zero_or_invalid_investment.

MUTATION_CONTRACT.non_vacuity_definition: A mutation control is non-vacuous only if applying the mutation to the real working tree makes at least one NAMED control fail, and if that control passes on the unmutated tree. A mutation that leaves the suite green proves the guarded assertion does not exist, and is itself a BLOCKING finding for the implementation node.

execution_obligations.real_bytes: Each mutation MUST be applied to real working-tree bytes and then restored byte-exactly. A mutation reasoned about but never applied does not discharge its control.
execution_obligations.pristine_capture_ordering: Capture the pristine copy of every file to be mutated BEFORE the first edit of the sequence, never inside the edit loop. Capturing a pristine copy after an earlier mutation has landed poisons the restore baseline and makes byte-exact restoration unverifiable.
execution_obligations.restoration_proof: Restoration is proven by hashing each mutated file before the first edit and after the final restore and comparing the two digests, and by confirming a clean `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` at the end of the mutation sequence. A visual re-read is not proof.
execution_obligations.chunking: The mutation sequence MUST be chunked so that no single command invocation can be interrupted mid-control. An interrupted run can leave a mutation on disk, which silently converts the working tree into a mutated tree for every subsequent gate.
execution_obligations.scope: Mutations may touch only the five authorized paths. A mutation that would require editing a sixth path is out of scope and its control must be redesigned within the five.

TENANCY_DISPOSITION.ownership: PF1 does NOT own the Portfolio tenancy coupling successor and does not need it in order to implement the five authorized files.
TENANCY_DISPOSITION.rule: PF1 must not touch the three Portfolio pages' unauthenticated / no-selection auth branches. The prohibition is unconditional and does not depend on who eventually owns them; the parent records the owner as TO_BE_MAPPED.
TENANCY_DISPOSITION.structural_reason_pf1_is_unaffected: All three prohibited branches live in app/app/portfolios/**, and no path under app/ appears in PF1_WRITE_SURFACE. The prohibition is enforced by the write surface itself, not only by intent.
TENANCY_DISPOSITION.organization_binding_pf1_relies_on: PF1 reads the caller's organization through getCurrentOrganizationContext(), already imported at lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:12 and called at :152. PF1 introduces no new tenancy mechanism, no new principal resolution and no RLS dependency. The parent's retracted_prediction_S3_rls key records that Portfolio has NO RLS dependency on S3 and must not manufacture one; PF1 manufactures none.

LOCKS.protected_grant_measured_basis: scripts/ods-scope.ts:82-90 declares DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS as docs/ops/fib/**, docs/ops/pc01b/**, docs/ops/im01b/**, db/migrations/**, db/prepared/**, db/baseline/** and docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json. Neither docs/ops/portfolio/** nor any of the five PF1 implementation paths matches any of these, so no --protected-authority grant is required for this authority mission or for the PF1 implementation node.
LOCKS.migration_measured_basis: The parent records that Portfolio consumes no migration ordinal, no journal wrapper ordinal and no baseline unit ordinal, and explicitly does not allocate 0067 or any later ordinal. PF1 touches no file under db/, so it cannot consume one.

implementation_lock.release: Released as soon as the disposable container is torn down. The lock is not held across the whole implementation node.
implementation_lock.not_taken_by_this_mission: The present authority-only mission takes NO lock. It runs no PostgreSQL of any kind — HEAVY_PG_REQUIRED is false on the parent and remains false here.

resolution_of_the_integrated_field.corroborating_fields: PORTFOLIO_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS = 'NOT_STARTED — no implementation is authorized by this mission or by the R1 correction'; GRANT_ID = null; authority_class = 'PRODUCT_AUTHORITY'.
resolution_of_the_integrated_field.reading: The integrated product authority froze the future implementation surfaces — it enumerated the PF1, PF2 and PF3 path sets and the product decisions that govern them — but it did not itself grant write permission to anyone. Its false value is therefore a statement about ITS OWN grant, not a prohibition that this successor contradicts.

This artifact is integrated into integration/commercial-v1.

MEASURED_BASELINE_OF_THE_IMPLEMENTATION_.purpose: Record the live pre-PF1 state of lib/portfolios/analytics.ts at AS_OF_TREE, so that an audit of the PF1 implementation node can distinguish what PF1 changed from what it inherited, and so that the mutation controls' non-vacuity claims are checkable against a fixed baseline.

measured_facts.fact: ExcludedProject.reason is the three-member union 'no_run' | 'non_usd_currency' | 'no_sroi_ratio'. Three of the six frozen reasons are absent.
PortfolioAggregate.included carries three fields — projectId, projectName, sroiRatio. Six of the nine traceability fields are absent, including runId and reviewId.
The run query filters on projectId IN (...), organizationId and status = 'calculated'. There is NO approval predicate of any kind.

Latest-run-per-project selection takes the first row per projectId from a version DESC, calculated_at DESC ordering. Because no approval filter has been applied, an unapproved newest run currently wins.

Reviews are fetched for the already-selected runs only, filtered on calculationRunId IN (...) and organizationId, with NO status filter — so a draft, reviewed, flagged or archived review can currently supply the readiness value — and ordered by desc(reviewedAt), the prohibited column.

toProjectRunSummaryRun returns null when investment or net parses to null, which classifies the project as no_run at :65-67. Zero and negative investments are not rejected at all and reach the denominator at :81.
Imports are decimal.js, drizzle-orm, @/db/client, @/db/schema, @/lib/auth/session. No readiness_assessments and no getReadinessAssessment — NEG-READINESS-1 is GREEN today.

readinessSource is the literal 'LEGACY_NON_AUTHORITATIVE'; averageLegacyManualReadinessScore and legacyManualReadinessCoverage are computed over included projects carrying a score. All four B5 symbol names are live and correct.

Twelve existing assertions across two describe blocks, including the Sigma/Sigma-not-average control at :25, the no_sroi_ratio controls at :107 and :133, and the LEGACY_NON_AUTHORITATIVE labelling control at :83. PF1 extends this file; it may not weaken or delete any of these.

MEASURED_BASELINE_OF_THE_IMPLEMENTATION_.implication: PF1 is a substantive correction, not a cosmetic one: at AS_OF_TREE the approved-run population, the six-reason exclusion vocabulary, the nine-field traceability tuple and the review tie-break are all absent or wrong on the live path.

VALIDATION_PERFORMED_BY_THIS_MISSION.scope_note: These are the gates of the AUTHORITY-ONLY mission. The implementation node's own exit gates are listed under MANIFEST_DISPOSITION.exit_gates_inherited_from_batch_manifest and are NOT discharged here.
VALIDATION_PERFORMED_BY_THIS_MISSION.json_validation: The artifact parses as JSON via JSON.parse and re-serializes without loss. Structural self-consistency of its own cross-references is asserted in self_check.

schema_applicability.repository_json_schemas_measured: Exactly one JSON Schema artifact exists in the repository: docs/ops/ods/UELLIX_TEST_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_v1.0.0.json. `find docs -iname '*SCHEMA*'` otherwise returns only two prose audit documents.
schema_applicability.proof: That schema declares required = [manifest_id, node_or_batch, exit_gates, positive_controls, negative_controls] and additionalProperties = false. This artifact has ZERO of those five keys at top level — its control blocks are nested inside PF1_NEW_CONTROLS, never hoisted — and carries 39 top-level keys the schema would forbid. It therefore does not claim, and cannot be read as claiming, to be a test manifest.
schema_applicability.consistency_with_precedent: COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_CE1_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json likewise declares neither manifest_id nor node_or_batch. Execution authorities are not schema-governed in this repository; test manifests are.
schema_applicability.consequence: The JSON/schema validation gate is discharged by parse validity plus the cross-artifact and self-consistency checks recorded here, because no schema binds this artifact class. Had this mission materialized a second, companion test manifest, that manifest WOULD have been bound by UELLIX_TEST_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_v1.0.0.json — one further reason the single-artifact form is the honest one.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: The integrated batch manifest and the integrated product authority name different PostgreSQL file paths for PF1.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_V1_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json's postgres_requirements names tests/postgres/portfolio-v1.setup.json and tests/postgres/portfolio-v1.probes.json. PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json's authorized_future_implementation_surface.PF1_tests names tests/postgres/portfolio-aggregate.pg.test.ts and tests/postgres/portfolio-aggregate.probes.json. Neither of the manifest's two names exists at AS_OF_TREE, and no *setup.json exists anywhere under tests/postgres/.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: The product authority enumerates the authorized WRITE SURFACE, which is the operative question for an execution grant, and it is the artifact the parent's own next_gate points at. The manifest's postgres_requirements is a pointer to intended fixtures, not a write-surface enumeration. The divergence is resolvable without guessing.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE PRODUCT AUTHORITY, in POSTGRES_CONTRACT.file_resolution. Neither integrated artifact is edited. Recorded here so that an auditor encounters the divergence as a disclosed finding rather than as an unexplained deviation from the manifest.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: The live review query applies no review-status filter at all.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:215-220 filters reviews only on calculationRunId and organizationId. sroi_run_reviews.status admits draft, reviewed, approved, flagged and archived (db/schema.ts:931), so a draft or archived review can currently supply the displayed legacy readiness value.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: PF1's approved-run population and approved-review tie-break both require a status = 'approved' predicate, so implementing this authority closes the gap as a consequence. It is recorded because it is a distinct defect from the reviewed_at ordering defect and an auditor should see both named.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Closed by APPROVED_RUN_CONTRACT.required_predicates and APPROVED_REVIEW_TIEBREAK when PF1 is implemented. No separate control is added; PF1-POS-TIEBREAK-1's fixture requirement exercises it.

OPEN_FINDINGS.title: sroi_calculation_runs (project_id, version) uniqueness is invisible in db/schema.ts.
OPEN_FINDINGS.detail: uq_sroi_run_project_version is created in db/migrations/0029_integrity.sql:6-7 and is absent from the Drizzle constraint array at db/schema.ts:855-858.
OPEN_FINDINGS.why_non_blocking: The uniqueness is real and is what makes run selection by version DESC total. Nothing needs to change.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Recorded as a reviewer hazard in APPROVED_RUN_CONTRACT.determinism_of_run_selection.reader_hazard, so that an auditor verifying determinism against the schema module alone does not raise a false finding.
